# AI Enabled Knowledge Wiki

Getting real work done with AI tools at the access tier you actually have.

HOW TO USE THIS FILE. This is a manifest, not the content. Find the one to three
pages that bear on your question, then fetch only those files. Do not fetch the
whole repository.

VERIFICATION. Two separate fields, two separate questions.

  method = how strongly the CLAIMS are backed
    vendor-documented = from docs, nobody executed it        (confidence: low)
    agent-executed    = an LLM ran the test, nondeterministic (confidence: max medium)
    script-verified   = a deterministic test passed           (confidence: max high)
    human-executed    = a person did it against the live tool (confidence: max high)

  reviewed = whether the WRITING was checked
    none | llm-reviewed | human-reviewed

A page can be well reviewed and completely unverified. That is the normal state
for anything needing a live account, and it is stated rather than hidden.

Report the method when you cite a procedure. When the method is agent-executed
or script-verified, also report the scope limit the page states: a test proves
something narrower than the procedure it belongs to.

last_reviewed: null means no human has read the page. Such a page is not stale,
because it was never fresh. It is unreviewed, which is a stronger caveat.

Schema: SCHEMA.md   Routing rules: CLAUDE.md


## Tools

One page per tool and access tier.

- `tools/copilot-free.md` — **Microsoft Copilot (free consumer tier)** [UNREVIEWED]: Microsoft Copilot's free consumer tier is a web-based AI chat assistant, available at no cost in a browser, in desktop and mobile apps, and inside Edge.

## Learning paths

Ordered sequences. Start here if unsure where to begin.

- `paths/free-tier-starter.md` — **Free-tier starter path** [UNREVIEWED]: A new ops-analyst — someone with free-tier tooling only who needs to make one recurring task repeatable this week.

## Patterns

Tool-agnostic approaches.

- `patterns/generated-single-file-tool.md` — **Generated single-file tool (the model emits the software)** [intermediate, UNREVIEWED]: A small but real piece of software — a payback calculator, a checklist, a unit converter — would traditionally need a developer, a hosting decision, or admin rights to deploy.
- `patterns/portable-prompt-template.md` — **Portable prompt template (carry the skill as a file)** [basic, UNREVIEWED]: On a tier with no saved skills, no reusable projects, and no persistent memory worth building on, every run of a recurring task starts from scratch.

## Procedures

Step-by-step, tool-specific. Check verification.method before trusting.

- `procedures/apply-prompt-file-to-data-file.md` — **Apply a prompt file to a data file in one conversation** [intermediate, vendor-documented/low, llm-reviewed, on copilot-free, UNREVIEWED]: Applying a standard check to a new dataset without a saved skill (copilot-free limitation 2) means getting both the instructions and the data into one conversation.
- `procedures/build-roi-calculator-copilot-free.md` — **Build a single-file ROI calculator with free Copilot** [intermediate, script-verified/high, llm-reviewed, on copilot-free, UNREVIEWED]: The free tier includes no way to build or host an application — copilot-free limitation 1, a web-based general assistant with no development or deployment surface — so generated-si
- `procedures/create-data-audit-prompt-block.md` — **Create a reusable data-audit prompt block** [basic, agent-executed/medium, llm-reviewed, on copilot-free, UNREVIEWED]: The free tier documents no way to save a reusable skill inside the product (copilot-free limitation 2), so a recurring data-quality review is otherwise re-derived from memory each
- `procedures/share-prompt-blocks-with-team.md` — **Distribute prompt blocks to a team without a paid tier** [basic, vendor-documented/low, llm-reviewed, on copilot-free, UNREVIEWED]: The free tier has no shared skill library, so a block one person refined stays on that person's machine (copilot-free limitation 2).

## Concepts

How and why things work.

- `concepts/system-prompt.md` — **The system prompt (a fixed instruction block)** [basic, UNREVIEWED]: A system prompt is a block of standing instructions — the role to play, the rules to follow, and the output format to return — placed at the start of a conversation so that every l

## Roles

Who material is written for.

- `roles/ops-analyst.md` — **Operations analyst (free-tier tooling only)** [UNREVIEWED]: Someone who runs recurring operational analysis — quality checks, summaries, small calculations — as part of another job.
- `roles/team-lead.md` — **Team lead (distributing a method, not doing the task)** [UNREVIEWED]: Someone accountable for how a team performs a recurring operation.
